comment: The runbooks as an inventory: every section of docs/35, docs/36 and docs/37, classified by how it is performed. Read by ops/runbook-verify.py (rule D6) and printed by tests/acceptance/runbook-drill.sh. Adding a section to one of those documents fails the drill until it is classified here — that is the point: a step nobody has said how to perform is the gap this task exists to find.

kinds.mechanised: a command performs this step; the command resolves in the tree and a corpus document names it
kinds.named-unavailable: a command performs this step and resolves, but the step cannot run yet; blocked_by names the tree claim that says why (ops/runbook-steps.json § tree_claims)
kinds.manual: a person performs it with no command in the runbooks
kinds.provider: an external service or credential performs it (the PostgreSQL provider, the object store, CI)
kinds.absent: nothing in the runbooks or the tree performs it yet

declared_gaps.marker: 开发环境完成 P0 后应支持
declared_gaps.reason: The document declares this block to be the target interface — the commands the environment is supposed to support once P0 is complete — and several of them (make test-e2e, rddev doctor as a CLI) do not exist yet. It is not a claim about today's tree, and the exclusion is checked: delete the marker sentence and the block is enforced again.

steps.note: Nine prerequisites — domain, TLS, Postgres, Redis, S3, Gitea, SMTP/Email provider, OIDC credentials, secret manager — that an operator obtains and verifies before step 1. Most of them are provider accounts whose credentials docs/25 § 发布 forbids the development system to hold, and the tree contains neither a command that provisions any of them nor one that checks they are present: the deployment template only names the variables they have to fill (ops/deploy/staging.env.example). This section was invisible to the inventory until the section pattern covered `## ` headings, which is exactly the kind of silently unclassified step this file exists to prevent.

The tree has no production backup entry point: the only backup-shaped thing in it is the restore drill (ops/backup-restore-drill.sh), which restores into an empty environment rather than taking a scheduled production dump. ops/deploy/README.md § What is missing #3 names that gap and its owner, so this step is the PostgreSQL provider's backup today.

The service, its depends_on ordering and its restart: "no" all exist (ops/deploy/README.md step 2); the image does not, and neither does the migration runner the image is supposed to contain (ops/deploy/README.md § What is missing #2).

steps.command: docker compose -f ops/deploy/docker-compose.staging.yml up -d --wait api worker mcp adapter
steps.note: The template starts four services here, not three: ops/deploy/README.md step 3 adds the scientific adapter to docs/35's API/worker/MCP. That is an addition, not a contradiction — docs/35 fixes the order, the template fixes the service list.

steps.command: docker compose -f ops/deploy/docker-compose.staging.yml up -d --wait web proxy
steps.note: The proxy comes up last on purpose: it is the only published surface and it waits for the API and the web app to report healthy.

An operator checks that Gitea can reach the API's webhook endpoint (the compose file defaults it to http://api:8080/api/v1/git/hooks/gitea). There is no command in the runbooks that performs the check, and a webhook Gitea cannot reach is accepted and never delivered.

steps.anchor: 6. 检查 object storage bucket policy/CORS。
steps.note: Bucket policy and CORS live in the object-storage account, not in this tree: the local stack's infra/docker/init.sh configures the DEV MinIO bucket and is not a staging mechanism. ops/deploy/README.md step 6 names what has to hold (CORS for POST_WEB_ORIGIN).

ops/deploy/README.md step 7 gives the three curl commands; /healthz and /readyz are routes cmd/api really mounts, so the command is well-formed — there is simply no deployment to point it at. The eight check areas of the runbook are broader than the three endpoints the template documents.

The canonical minimal E2E is task T1202 (canonical MOF workflow E2E), which is not merged. The feature-shaped browser suites under tests/e2e-*/** exist, but no command runs the canonical workflow end to end.

Two halves. The application half is the documented digest revert (ops/deploy/README.md § Rollback) and needs a running deployment. The database half — "DB 只 forward repair" — is re-derived from the tree by rule T2 and executed for real, against PostgreSQL, by tests/acceptance/runbook-recovery (restore an older schema version, repair forward to head, and a rollback attempt that must move nothing).

`make ci` (bash scripts/ci.sh) reproduces the workflow's stage list locally, in the same order. The authoritative blocking run is .github/workflows/ci.yml on GitHub, whose job list this command is kept in step with by hand — a local green is evidence about the same gates, not proof the remote run happened.

Migration half: docs/36 names no command. The tree's mechanisms are `make check-schema-snapshot` (migrations still equal the canonical schema), `make check-schema-drift` and the migration-integration CI job, which applies the set to a real pgvector PostgreSQL — none of them is named by this runbook.

Changelog: the repository has no CHANGELOG file and no convention for one. Feature flags: no flag mechanism exists in the tree (no feature-flag table, loader or env). Security scan: the secret scan exists as a Go test (internal/config TestRepoExampleFilesAreSecretFree) and is run by the deployment smoke gate, but there is no dependency/CVE scan and CI has no security job — docs/25_CICD_DEVOPS.md item 9 asks for one.

Two gaps, not one: there is no staging environment to run against (no images — tree claim no-dockerfile, ops/deploy/README.md § What is missing #1), and the canonical E2E is T1202, not merged. tests/acceptance/deploy-staging-smoke.sh checks the staging template statically and does not stand in for this step.

Nothing builds an image: there is no Dockerfile, and CI has no container build/SBOM stage (docs/25 item 10). What does exist is the rule that consumes the digest — the staging validator refuses an image pinned by anything but @sha256:<64 hex> (rule R03), and the compose file refuses to interpret without one.

The same smoke command as the deployment runbook's step 7, and beyond the missing images there is no production environment at all — a production deploy also needs credentials the development system is forbidden to hold (docs/25 § 发布).

steps.anchor: - 观察 error/queue/outbox/git drift 30min 的指标窗口（自动/人工可按环境）。
steps.note: docs/26_OBSERVABILITY.md defines the signals (errors, queue depth, outbox lag, git drift); nothing in the tree opens a 30-minute window on them, and the runbook itself allows this to be automatic or by hand depending on the environment.

steps.anchor: - 失败按 deployment runbook rollback/forward fix。
steps.note: The same two halves as docs/35 § 回滚: the application rolls back to the previous digest (needs images), the database only moves forward (re-derived by rule T2, executed by tests/acceptance/runbook-recovery).

The drill covers the four classes docs/37 names — PostgreSQL, S3 blobs/manifests, Gitea repositories, critical secrets/config metadata — and refuses the run if a credential value reaches the artifacts. It is an exercise of the process, not a scheduled production backup (deploy-1-db-backup).

The drill reconciles the four axes docs/37 names — DB ↔ Git refs ↔ blob hashes ↔ release manifests — and records the snapshot timestamp. It reports drift and never repairs it: findings land in the audit log, repairs_applied stays 0.

The empty-environment restore is the run's own subject: the drill proves the target is empty (0 tables, no bucket, no organization) before writing anything, then opens Seed Project, Release, Asset, Files and Evidence Graph on the restored environment.
No RPO or RTO is measured, asserted or claimed anywhere: docs/37 puts V1's acceptance at "the process runs", and the drill prints that it measures neither.

tree_claims.anchor: There is no `Dockerfile` anywhere in this repository
tree_claims.note: The claim every "cannot deploy yet" statement rests on. When a Dockerfile lands, this check fails and the inventory's named-unavailable steps have to be revisited — which is the intent.

tree_claims.anchor: The worker has no healthcheck, deliberately
tree_claims.note: Why the compose file carries a healthcheck waiver for the worker instead of a probe. If cmd/worker grows an HTTP surface, this check fails, the waiver becomes stale, and the template's own validator already refuses a stale waiver.

tree_claims.anchor: the Go loader has no `*_FILE` support
tree_claims.note: Why the runbook does not use Compose's secrets: mechanism — a file-mounted secret would look configured and reach nothing. Add *_FILE support to the loader and this check fails, so the runbook has to be revisited rather than quietly describing the old loader.
